I already checked for a Blender installation, found none, and kicked off a background snap install. Unfortunately that install hit a permission snag (“error: access denied (try with sudo)”) and fell back to a tarball plan, which I haven’t yet executed. So at this moment I still don’t have Blender available in the environment.

Given that, I need to decide what concrete step I can take right now that moves the project forward without waiting for a successful Blender install. The user also wants me to “look at assets in game via screenshots so you can properly enhance them.” Earlier I drafted a small Node script, visual‑audit.mjs, that launches the game server, opens a headless Chromium instance via puppeteer, navigates to each asset (weapons, maps, UI elements), and saves screenshots into a dedicated audit folder. I wrote that file to /home/lane/AIArchives/archives/neonstrike/test/visual-audit.mjs and verified it was saved.

Now the logical next move is to actually execute that script so I can collect the screenshots. Running the script will spin up the server (which the script does via spawn), then puppeteer will drive the browser to capture the assets. Once it finishes, I’ll have a set of images in ../playtest/audit that I (or the user) can inspect to decide what needs visual enhancement. Since the script may take a while—starting the server, waiting for it to be ready, loading pages, taking screenshots—I should give it a generous timeout. Five minutes (300 000 ms) should be more than enough for the whole audit to complete, even on a modest CI box.

I also want to keep the output manageable. The script prints a fair amount of log information (server start messages, puppeteer navigation logs, etc.). Rather than dump the entire log into the conversation, I’ll pipe the output through `tail -5` so I only see the last few lines, which typically include a summary or a “done” message. That gives the user a quick confirmation that the audit ran to completion without overwhelming them.

Therefore, the appropriate next action is a Bash tool call that changes directory into the test folder, runs `node visual-audit.mjs`, captures both stdout and stderr, pipes through `tail -5`, and sets a timeout of 300 000 ms. This will produce the immediate feedback I need and set the stage for the next visual‑upgrade steps once I have the screenshots (and once Blender is finally installed).

So I’ll issue that command now.
